speakers: Richard Brennan (guest, systematic trend-following manager and researcher)
summary: Brennan and Niels review the August 2024 volatility shock and trend-following performance, then Brennan argues backtests overfit and recommends walk-forward out-of-sample testing (OOS drawdowns 35-40% versus 5-10% in backtests); that trends come from trader impact feedback (divergent vs convergent forces, cocoa example) so AI will not end them; and that highly correlated markets can still diversify outlier-hunting ensemble models via trade correlation.

coverage.note: intro; Aug 2024 vol event and trend followers' adaptation
CTA forced-selling estimates, vol-driven positioning, turbulence analogy
convergence strategies break, carry creep, psychology, look-back, volatility dampening
research caution, August sector performance, diversification, intramonth vol
VIX vs futures, trend barometer, August index numbers
backtest vs walk-forward, hindsight, selection bias
statistical bias, overfit, walk-forward design, benchmark with live managers
regime expectation, OOS drawdown, realism, adaptive process
three curves, mean reversion vs trend validation, in-sample size
contaminating OOS, data mining; AI and trends, trader impact
square-root law, collective impact, nonstationary mix, divergent vs convergent
three market structures, style switching, crowded trend followers, mean reversion dissipation
cocoa example, endogenous vs exogenous, AI and trends
AI cannot end trends; correlated markets and outlier hunters
ensembles, butterfly effect, cocoa, VaR crowding

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: we got slapped slapped around by the Japanese Yen and um the NASDAQ coming off and the S&P 500 coming off
claims.claim: In early August 2024 a sharp volatility event (yen carry unwind, Nasdaq and S&P drop) hurt trend followers, but it reversed quickly and trends resumed.
claims.direction: trend followers lose on sharp reversals
claims.conditions: short sharp event followed by reversal

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the good thing about our models is they they're very quick to adapt
claims.claim: Trend models adapt quickly: had the sell-off become a prolonged downtrend they would have adjusted and been well positioned.
claims.testable: yes - trend following in drawdown regimes

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: that usually makes us become a little bit more defensive in our positioning
claims.claim: A quick volatile event makes vol-scaled trend followers more defensive in positioning, so the next shock hurts less; expect performance dispersion and model speed to matter.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: oh CT have to sell 170 billion I think was the number of equities
claims.claim: Sell-side estimates of forced CTA equity selling ($170B) are misleading: CTAs may keep selling after a rebound if volatility stays higher, and do not simply buy everything back.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: even if the markets bounce back we might be selling still because it's more volatile so we need to adjust positions
claims.claim: Volatility-targeted trend followers reduce exposure after a vol rise even if prices recover.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: none of the planes have any structural damage
claims.claim: Analogy: severe turbulence hurts those inside but not the structure; similarly trend-following drawdowns are painful but do not break the models.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's very hard for me to imagine that any Market event would break a trend following system unless you start doing things you shouldn't do
claims.claim: No market event breaks a rule-based trend system with sensible, tested rules (not AI-optimised); convergence strategies and systematic macro are the ones that tend to break.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: other strategies that I see do break are of course tend to be convergence strategies and even quote unquote these systematic macro strategies
claims.claim: Convergence strategies and systematic macro tend to break in turbulence, unlike trend following.
claims.testable: partly - strategy comparison in stress months

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there's always going to be a pressure from investors to uh either return better when there are no Trends but also to smooth out returns in general
claims.claim: Investor pressure pushes trend programs to add non-trend models such as carry to smooth returns, which dilutes the pure trend profile and may explain dispersion between managers.
claims.testable: yes - compare pure vs diversified trend programs

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: our models are incredibly robust but our ability out to our psychology to hold and and respect what these models do
claims.claim: The trend follower's weak point is psychology: overriding rules causes errors, so discipline and patience are required.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: I'm a big fan of sort of medium to long term I think all the data that I've seen suggest that is more robust in the long run and has performed better than shorter term
claims.claim: Medium to long-term trend following is more robust and has performed better than shorter-term trend following.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we're trying to find things that will dampen the uh Vol volatility of the prog which is what volatility adjusting is doing
claims.claim: Dampening volatility via volatility adjustment is like an aircraft stabiliser.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's fine if we can find things to improve and say lower the volatility or reduce the draw down as long as we don't change the profile and the perform long-term performance of the program
claims.claim: Risk-reducing research is acceptable only if it does not change the long-term return profile or cause style drift, otherwise it just lowers expectations.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: equities have been the most challenging sector for for Trend followers by quite a margin
claims.claim: In August 2024 equities were the hardest sector for trend followers, currencies (yen) difficult, fixed income divided, while sugar, coffee and grains trended well.
claims.direction: equities losses, softs and grains gains

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: just the importance of true diversification in a portfolio if you're too heav heavy on financials because you want to have massive AUM
claims.claim: True diversification into commodities matters; managers concentrated in financials (to hold large AUM) suffered more in the month.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: if you analyze things on a month-by-month basis you won't see this intram month volatility and that's a bit deceptive
claims.claim: Monthly industry statistics hide intra-month volatility, so a month with a severe shock can look benign in the record.
claims.testable: yes - compare daily vs monthly drawdowns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: did the vix really hit 65 or you know because the Futures didn't the Futures didn't hit 65
claims.claim: The VIX cash spike to about 65 was not matched by VIX futures; the spike subsided very quickly back to low-vol conditions, like a fast news cycle.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it finished at 61 yesterday
claims.claim: Trend Barometer (short timeframe) recovered to 61 in late August after the early-month shock, mirroring the quick recovery (but the app stopped updating).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: beta 50 is down still 1.7% up 3.4% for the year sock gen CG index down 2.6 6% in August up 3.4% for the year
claims.claim: August 2024 data: Beta 50 -1.7% (+3.4% YTD), SG CTA -2.6% in August, SG Trend -3.55% (+2.3% YTD), short-term traders +0.61%, so industry recovered less than managers Brennan and Niels know.
claims.indicator: Beta 50, SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short Term Traders

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the S&P 500 total return up about 1% in August up 17.8% so far this year
claims.claim: August 2024 traditional markets: MSCI World +1% (+13.84% YTD), global sovereign bonds +1% (+1.58% YTD), S&P 500 TR +1% (+17.8% YTD).

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the back test process actually significantly introduces over fitting into the process
claims.claim: Backtests significantly introduce overfitting, with marked differences between backtest and walk-forward/out-of-sample results.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: with a back test when you've got the history laid out you know every deviation all in hindsight you've got the benefit of This Magnificent hindsight position
claims.claim: Live trading is on the right-hand side of the chart with no hindsight; backtests give hindsight advantage, as do macro causal narratives given after the event.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: back testing is useful for doing things like um undertaking sensitivity tests on your models
claims.claim: Backtests are useful for sensitivity tests across simulated regimes but should never be used to predict future expected returns because they are always overfit.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: you've got 10 parameter choices and your results are 10 different return streams
claims.claim: Selection bias: with ten parameter settings, choosing the best-looking stream uses hindsight selection and biases the forward expectation.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: biasing your result that's what we call a statistical bias associated with a hindsight selection process
claims.claim: Choosing among alternatives with hindsight introduces statistical bias that cannot occur in live trading and should not be done in backtests.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: your back test is inevitably going to overfit to that perfect scenario that's laid down
claims.claim: A backtest overfits to noise and every past event as the full road map is known, whereas the future order of events is unknown.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: a far better way to undertake testing for anticipating what your future performance is going to be is what I'm referring to as a walk forward using out of sample data
claims.claim: Use walk-forward out-of-sample testing: develop in-sample (e.g. 1970-2000), then test untouched out of sample (2000-2024) to anticipate live drawdown and performance.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: you have tainted that data once you've used it you can never use it again
claims.claim: Once data is used for development and robustness testing it is tainted and cannot serve as out-of-sample.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: you can Benchmark that against the live track records of other fund managers and lo and behold you're going to find it's very similar
claims.claim: An out-of-sample equity curve is close to live track records of other managers, unlike the glorious backtest.
claims.indicator: out-of-sample vs live manager track records

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: you've got to have a favorable Trend following regime for your Trend following models to be working
claims.claim: Trend following depends on regime; in an unfavorable regime expect stagnation and drawdowns, so expect a volatile equity curve, not a straight line.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the back test draw down is going to say 10% 5% or something the the outer sample draw down is going to say 35% 40% something
claims.claim: Out-of-sample drawdown is far larger (35-40%) than the backtest drawdown (5-10%), giving a realistic benchmark for maximum drawdown, CAGR and volatility.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: you never see a bad um back test and the reality is you want to see a bad you want to see realism you want to see realism
claims.claim: Backtests shown publicly (e.g. on Twitter) are beautiful equity curves; one should demand realism.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: you might have an Adaptive proc built in where you might use a insample component from 1970 up to 2000 and then periodically you might um do do a walk forward
claims.claim: An adaptive workflow periodically re-estimates in-sample and walks forward, and the result should be compared with the static model on the same period.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: recognizing that the back test Equity curve is always going to be far superior than the other models
claims.claim: Compare three curves (backtest 'pink unicorn', out-of-sample, adaptive); the backtest is always the best but unrealistic.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: but in our world of trend following we never know when the next Trends are going to be so we don't have that luxury of assuming that The Continuous trajectory going on into the future
claims.claim: Mean reversion modellers expect no out-of-sample deterioration after finding a pattern, but trend followers cannot, because trends arrive irregularly with favorable and unfavorable regimes.
claims.testable: partly - contrasts mean reversion vs trend validation

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: clearly they're going to be showing some uh type of of back tested results which are you know unlikely to be uh uh reproduced in the future for sure
claims.claim: Social-media backtest results are unlikely to reproduce; big managers use some walk-forward process.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: you might decide that um multimarket testing um is the way to develop robustness
claims.claim: In-sample development needs a lot of data for robustness; multi-market testing over 30 years and 100 markets provides it.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: that's really starting to interfere with that that process and contaminating um your process with statistical bias
claims.claim: Selecting or changing models after seeing out-of-sample results contaminates the test with statistical bias; people underestimate how sensitive results are to overfitting.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: never never touch that out of sample data that's gold to you
claims.claim: Avoid data-mining packages that overfit and then remove it afterwards (Monte Carlo etc.); never touch out-of-sample data so you do not need to extract overfitting later.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: Trends are are omnipresent in any complex adaptive system
claims.claim: Trends exist in any complex adaptive system, so human behavioural bias (prospect theory) is a symptom, not the root cause.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: I'd like to suggest that it's actually Trader impacts that is responsible for Trends and mean reversion in the financial markets
claims.claim: Trends and mean reversion arise from trader impact: orders that must be matched and that exert pressure on price, not from news, fundamentals or human behaviour per se.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: it follows a square root law larger orders have more gravitas more impact in the market than smaller orders
claims.claim: Market impact follows a square-root law (Bouchaud), a nonlinear relation between order size and price impact.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: it's the aggregated effect of all of these Trader impacts the collective impact of all of that which is responsible for moving price
claims.claim: Groups of traders (trend followers, mean reverters, fundamentals, HFT) exert collective forces, and their combination moves price.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: this this Trader impact changes over the course of time the the relative mix of participants doing a similar thing changes
claims.claim: Markets are nonstationary: the mix of participant groups changes as traders enter and leave, so the balance of divergent and convergent pressure shifts.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: we can start looking at two different pressures that are working in the market Divergent pressures those that are amplifying each other
claims.claim: Divergent pressures (positive feedback) amplify trends and convergent pressures (negative feedback) dissipate trend signals.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: but there is a third class of Market structure which is noise which is when the convergent and Divergent neither win there's a battle going on
claims.claim: Three market structures: divergent wins (trend), convergent wins (mean reversion), or noise when neither wins and there is no directional move.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: I'm going to change my style from mean reversion or high frequency trade whatever I'm going to jump on board that Trend
claims.claim: Participants switch style to join strong trends, amplifying the signal, so the mix moves toward divergent behaviour in strong trends.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: if there are too many Trend followers in the market TR Trends get more extreme because everyone is doing the same thing
claims.claim: Too many trend followers does not kill trend following; it makes trends more extreme because their impact is collectively amplifying.
claims.testable: yes - compare trend returns vs AUM

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: to apply convergence you're usually commencing from a Divergent premise in other words price has made an Excursion away from an equilibrium
claims.claim: Convergence (mean reversion) signals fight a prior trend, so the mean reverter's edge dissipates when enough of them oppose the trend (and the trend signal dissipates if they win).

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: selling 80 85 90% of their notional position simply because the volatility was picking up
claims.claim: Cocoa 2024 example: trend followers who size dynamically sold 80-90% of notional Jan-May as volatility rose.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: so they started buying Coco in March right at the same time we were selling but initially that maybe with other people carried the price higher actually even though Trend followers were selling
claims.claim: Global macro funds bought cocoa as trend followers sold in March 2024, carrying the price higher before a roughly 40% correction.
claims.indicator: cocoa; macro fund buying vs CTA selling

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: endogenous forces are actually much more responsible for uh big moves than the exogenous which is like news events and stuff like that
claims.claim: Bouchaud's conclusion: endogenous forces (flows) explain big moves more than exogenous news.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the acceleration of that Trend was certainly I think attributed to endogenous forces
claims.claim: For cocoa, supply news in Africa began the run but participants jumping on the bandwagon accelerated it, and large holders selling in April probably caused the sell-off.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: I think Trends and mean reversion are here to stay for eternity because I think that they're a universal symptom of how collect Dynamics working complex adaptive systems
claims.claim: AI agents also exert impact, so trends and mean reversion will persist; AI will not remove them.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: for nearly all models except the outly hunter I would say 100% correct however for the outly hunter I'd say Incorrect
claims.claim: Conventional wisdom that highly correlated markets add no diversification is correct for most models but not for 'outlier hunter' trend followers using ensembles of models.
claims.testable: yes - compare correlation of returns vs prices

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the important thing for the outlaw Hunter is not the price correlations it's the trade correlations
claims.claim: What matters is the correlation of strategy returns from trading each market, not price correlations.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: I find that their performance results their return streams are really quite uncorrelated
claims.claim: Applying the same ensemble to Brent and WTI gives quite uncorrelated return streams despite highly correlated prices.
claims.indicator: Brent vs WTI ensemble return correlation
claims.conditions: ensembles of trend models in outlier moves

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: what you find is that when you are in this nonlinear territory very small variations are sufficient cause significantly dispersed results
claims.claim: In nonlinear outlier territory, small differences in price paths lead to significantly dispersed trade results.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: if you apply a single system to an outlaw you're going to fail because it might Capture One Outlaw but it's going to be snagged out of a volatility move of one outlier
claims.claim: Outliers are volatile and need an ensemble of models to maximize extraction, since a single system is snagged by the volatility.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: this is the very small differences in initial state are sufficient to create significant um dispersion in the nonlinear mechanics that arises from that result
claims.claim: Butterfly effect: tiny initial differences create dispersed outcomes in tail events, so correlated markets can still diversify.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: I wouldn't have been selling into trend on Coco in 2024
claims.claim: An outlier hunter holds and pyramids a strong trend (cocoa 2024) and accepts the big give-back when it turns.
claims.direction: hold or add to outlier trends

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the answer is of course not everyone uses valued risk a lot of people do but not everyone and therefore it still works
claims.claim: Even if many managers use VaR-style risk models sensitive to volatility, not all do, so the market is not forced into synchronized selling.
